_comment: Catalog of all static UI strings in the project. Algorithm explainer card text (managed in src/lib/algorithm-explainer/algorithms/*.json) is excluded. Organized by usage (component/area). Placeholders use {name} format.

infoTooltip.title: Training Metrics
infoTooltip.content: Numbers logged each step to track how training is going (reward, loss, KL, etc.). Click a chip below to add or remove a metric from the chart.

reinforce.description: The original policy gradient method. Each token's log-probability is nudged up or down by (response reward − baseline).

ppo.description: Clips the probability ratio so each update stays close to the model before this update. Adds a learned value model to reduce noise in the training signal.

grpo.description: PPO variant with no separate value model. Each response's advantage is its reward compared to the average reward of its response group on the same prompt.

dapo.description: GRPO with asymmetric clipping (clip-higher) and dynamic prompt set refilling, designed for stable long-horizon RL training.

drgrpo.description: GRPO without std-normalization on advantages and without length-normalization on the loss, removing two biases.

detailPanel.emptyState: Click a step on the radial chart
detailPanel.noResponses: No response data for this step

infoTooltip.title: Optimization Objectives
infoTooltip.content: The model update happens in two stages. First, each token's contribution is combined into one step-level objective. Then the current model takes one small step in the direction that increases this objective.

tokenLevel.label: Token-level Objective
tokenLevel.description: How each token contributes to the model update.

stepLevel.label: Step-Level Objective
stepLevel.description: Token-level objectives across all responses are combined into one value. The current model takes one update step to push it higher.

rolloutTooltip.title: Rollout
rolloutTooltip.content: In a rollout the current model generates responses to the prompt set and a reward model scores them. A rollout can include several update steps, and the extra steps do not generate new responses but only recompute the token probabilities of the existing ones, which makes the importance ratio drift away from 1.

infoTooltip.title: Response Examples
infoTooltip.content: Responses generated by the current model for each prompt. Each row is one response, colored by how much each token contributed to the update.

tooltip.title: Reward
tooltip.content: A single number scored by the reward model for this response. The advantage each algorithm uses to update the model is built on top of it.
tooltip.hint: Higher reward → more likely to be reinforced.

responseTooltip.title: Response {n}
responseTooltip.content: One response generated by the current model for this prompt.

metrics._usage: Chart ring labels, chip label/popover (RadialChart.svelte), step metric panel tooltip (StepMetrics.svelte)

reward.def: Mean reward across all responses in this step. A single score for the current model's responses.
reward.hint: Expect an upward trend when training is going well.

reward_std.def: Standard deviation of rewards within a response group (group_reward_std in GRPO).
reward_std.hint: If 0, every response in the group got the same reward — advantage collapses to 0 and there is no learning signal.

policy_objective.def: The step-level objective the optimizer is maximizing (sign-flipped from its loss form). PPO/GRPO/DAPO surrogate after clipping.
policy_objective.hint: Trending up = the current model is improving on this step.

policy_loss.def: Sign-flipped step-level objective (the form many training logs report). Trending toward negative values means the current model is improving.
policy_loss.hint: Small magnitude (near 0) is stable. Large swings are a blow-up signal.

learning_rate.def: Optimizer learning rate for the current model.
learning_rate.hint: Typically flat after warmup, or follows a decay schedule.

response_length.def: Mean number of tokens in a response.
response_length.hint: Longer = more exploration. Sudden spikes may signal reward hacking.

kl.def: Mean KL divergence between the current model π and the reference model π_ref. A measure of how different the two distributions are.
kl.hint: If too large, the current model drifts far from the reference model — risk of collapse.

ref_kl.def: Reference-model KL (near-synonym of kl, named differently by some sources).

clip_fraction.def: Fraction of tokens whose PPO probability ratio fell outside the clip range.
clip_fraction.hint: If too high, consider adjusting learning rate or clip_eps.

grad_norm.def: Gradient norm of the parameter update.
grad_norm.hint: Spikes indicate instability. Clipping with max_norm is recommended.

entropy.def: Mean entropy of the current model's output distribution. Higher = more random / diverse sampling.
entropy.hint: Dropping too quickly means insufficient exploration.

value_loss.def: Regression loss of the value model. PPO only.

total_loss.def: Sum of policy-gradient + value + entropy regularization terms.

advantage_mean.def: Mean advantage across this step's responses.
advantage_mean.hint: Near 0 is normal. A strong skew to one side suggests a normalization issue.

advantage_std.def: Standard deviation of advantages across this step's responses.

return.def: Mean cumulative/discounted return. In GRPO it's nearly identical to advantage.

importance_sampling_ratio.def: Mean importance sampling ratio = exp(log_prob − old_log_prob). Tracks how much the current model differs from the model that generated the responses.
importance_sampling_ratio.hint: Drifting far from 1.0 means the current model has moved away from the model that produced these responses — gradient estimates become unreliable.

dynamic_sampling_pass_rate.def: Percentage of prompts that passed DAPO dynamic sampling (kept in the prompt set).
dynamic_sampling_pass_rate.hint: Near 100% = filter too loose. Near 0% = too strict.

baseline.def: REINFORCE baseline b — running estimate of expected reward (EMA). Subtracted from reward to form advantage = r − b.
baseline.hint: Tracks reward closely. Used for variance reduction in REINFORCE.
